title: Graphs I: BFS/DFS, Components, Topo (Depth Pass)
relevance: High (Second ladder: CF-style reachability tricks, bipartite orientation, functional graphs, complement BFS, and DAG/Kahn variants — the post-Striver skill of finding the graph, not recalling the template).
company_notes: OA/interview shapes: block hazards then check all goods can escape (Solve The Maze / Monsters-style preprocess + reachability; Amazon/Meta grid variants); friendship/shared skill ⇒ same group and min invites/teaches (Learning Languages / News Distribution CC counting); order tasks with two machine types/cool-down (Coprocessor dual ready-set Kahn; build-system/scheduler interviews); nearest opposite category from every index (reverse multi-source BFS / Nearest Opposite Parity — multi-source infection flipped).

phases.goal: Spot that the statement hides a standard BFS/DFS/CC/topo engine behind a rewrite (block, orient, complement, reverse, state expand, or outdeg-1 structure).

must_hit.point: Depth asks still use DFS/BFS/CC/topo engines, but statements hide them behind rewrites: wall bad neighbors then reachability; 2-color then orient; search the complement; expand state (turns / layer mod 3 / parity); or reverse edges and multi-source from targets.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names at least one rewrite family instead of only recalling a plain BFS/DFS template.

must_hit.point: Recognize when you must force a property before searching, when n is large but missing edges are few, when each node has out-degree 1, when ordering splits into two processor types, or when nearest opposite/special is asked from every node.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Maps the prompt to one of those cues (preprocess, complement, functional graph, dual Kahn, reverse multi-source).

must_hit.point: Functional-graph cue: every node has outdeg = 1, so each component is a cycle with trees feeding in.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says outdeg-1 / cycle-with-inbound-trees (Mouse Hunt shape).

probes: What in this statement tells you to rewrite the graph before running ordinary BFS/DFS/CC/topo?

hints.1: Look for a forced property, scarce missing edges, outdeg-1 nodes, two processor types, or nearest-special from every node.
hints.2: Ask whether you should block neighbors, 2-color then orient, search the complement, reverse edges, expand state, or treat a functional graph.
hints.3: If you must force a property before search, n is large with few missing edges, outdeg=1, dual machine types, or nearest opposite from every v — name the matching rewrite.

phases.goal: Choose the right depth-pass rewrite: block-then-BFS, bipartite orientation, complement traversal, reverse multi-source, functional-graph cycle work, dual Kahn, or state/layered BFS.

must_hit.point: Block-then-BFS: to forbid paths through bad cells, first wall every neighbor of a bad cell, then one reachability BFS (Solve The Maze) — do not dodge during search.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes preprocess-wall then single reachability check for goods.

must_hit.point: Bipartite orientation: undirected → direct every edge from color 0→1; impossible iff odd cycle (Graph Without Long Directed Paths).
must_hit.evidence_hint: 2-colors then orients low→high color; fails on odd cycle.

must_hit.point: Reverse multi-source BFS: for every v, nearest u with property P → BFS from all P-nodes on the reversed graph (Nearest Opposite Parity).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Builds reverse edges and seeds BFS from all property sinks.

must_hit.point: Complement / near-complete: never materialize n^2 edges; keep an unused-node set and skip only explicit forbidden neighbors (The Two Routes / 0-1 MST).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Traverses unused vertices skipping only listed adj, not a dense edge list.

must_hit.point: Dual Kahn: two ready-queues (scarce vs free); repeatedly drain the free side, then spend one scarce step (Coprocessor).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Same indegrees, two pop policies, count scarce sessions.

must_hit.point: State/layered BFS: node=(v,state) for turns used, hop parity, or layer mod 3 (Igor ≤2 turns; Hopscotch Addict length ≡0 mod 3).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Uses (v,state) instead of rebuilding a huge explicit graph.

probes: Walk through which rewrite you would apply for Solve The Maze, Graph Without Long Directed Paths, or Nearest Opposite Parity before coding BFS.

hints.1: Match the story to block, orient, reverse, complement, dual queues, or state expand.
hints.2: Ask whether bad cells need walls first, edges need 0→1 orientation, queries need reverse multi-source, or outdeg-1 needs cycle compression.
hints.3: Solve The Maze: wall neighbors then BFS; long directed paths: 2-color orient; Nearest Opposite Parity: reverse multi-source from parity sinks.

phases.goal: Show checkable skeletons: component aggregates, clique-CC test, functional-graph pipeline, state-BFS arrays, dual ready-queues, and complement unused-set traversal.

must_hit.point: Component aggregates: store comp_id[] + comp_size[] / edge count; answer per-cell or per-query in O(1) / O(deg) (The Labyrinth-style).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Precomputes ids/sizes then sums distinct neighboring components.

must_hit.point: Clique-CC check: a component with s nodes is a clique iff it has exactly binom(s,2) edges (Bear and Friendship Condition).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Compares edge count to binom(s,2) per component.

must_hit.point: Functional-graph pipeline: iterate unvisited → follow unique outs → detect cycle → process cycle then inbound trees; place the cheapest trap on each cycle (Mouse Hunt).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Follows outdeg-1 edges, answers on cycles only, trees need nothing extra.

must_hit.point: State BFS skeleton: queue of (node, state) + dist[node][state]; keep state domain tiny (≤3–5).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Shows dist indexed by node and small state, not a rebuilt explicit graph.

must_hit.point: Complement traversal: set/list of unused vertices; on visit, erase and only skip adj-of-current.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Maintains unused set and erases on visit while skipping forbidden neighbors.

must_hit.point: Dual ready-queues Kahn: same indegree updates, two pops policies; count how often you must open the scarce queue.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Drains free queue fully between scarce pops and counts scarce opens.

probes: How would you code the unused-node complement BFS or the Mouse Hunt cycle-trap pass without materializing a dense graph?

hints.1: Lean on precomputed component arrays, unused-set walks, or outdeg-1 follow loops.
hints.2: For aggregates store comp_id/comp_size; for functional graphs follow unique outs to the cycle; for complement erase from an unused set.
hints.3: Labyrinth: sum distinct neighbor comp sizes; Mouse Hunt: min on each cycle only; complement: unused set skip adj-of-current; Coprocessor: drain free then one scarce.

phases.goal: Justify why rewrites stay efficient: avoid n^2 materialization, O((n+m) log n) complement walks, and O(1)/O(deg) answers after CC precompute.

must_hit.point: Near-complete / complement graphs must not materialize n^2 edges; unused-node set traversal is the intended cost model.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Refuses dense adjacency and cites unused-set skipping of forbidden neighbors.

must_hit.point: Complement traversal with a set/list of unused vertices runs in O((n+m) log n).
must_hit.evidence_hint: States the O((n+m) log n) unused-set bound from the checklist.

must_hit.point: After storing comp_id[] and comp_size[], per-cell or per-query answers are O(1) / O(deg).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Credits precompute for constant or degree-local queries.

must_hit.point: State BFS keeps the state domain tiny (≤3–5) instead of rebuilding a huge explicit layered graph.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Argues small (v,state) product beats an explicit blow-up.

probes: Why is building the full complement adjacency illegal here, and what runtime does the unused-set walk claim?

hints.1: Think about n^2 edges versus iterating only missing/forbidden neighbors.
hints.2: Compare materializing the complement to an unused-vertex set with erase-on-visit.
hints.3: Never build n^2 edges; unused-set complement walk is O((n+m) log n); CC answers after precompute are O(1)/O(deg).

phases.goal: Catch depth-pass failure modes: searching without preprocess, dense complement builds, wrong cycle/tree handling, and non-standard visited rules.

must_hit.point: Trying to dodge bad cells during search instead of walling every bad neighbor first then running one reachability BFS.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Insists on block-then-BFS preprocess for Solve The Maze.

must_hit.point: Materializing n^2 complement edges instead of an unused-node set that skips only explicit forbidden neighbors.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Rejects dense complement construction for The Two Routes / 0-1 MST.

must_hit.point: On functional graphs, placing traps on inbound trees; trees feeding into a cycle need nothing extra — only the cycle needs the cheapest trap.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Answers only on cycles after compressing tree→cycle structure.

must_hit.point: Ice Cave–style grids: destination may be re-entered iff it has ≥2 open neighbors — a non-standard visited rule.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions special revisit condition on the destination cell.

must_hit.point: DAG DP/path counts must fail cleanly if Kahn yields <n nodes (cycle present).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Checks topo produced fewer than n nodes before trusting DP.

probes: What goes wrong if you dodge hazards mid-BFS, build the full complement, or trap every node in a functional graph?

hints.1: Depth bugs are usually wrong rewrite or wrong visited/cycle policy, not missing BFS.
hints.2: Check preprocess walls, unused-set complement, cycle-only traps, and special destination revisit.
hints.3: Solve The Maze: wall then BFS; complement: unused set not n^2; Mouse Hunt: min on cycle only; Ice Cave: ≥2 open neighbors to re-enter destination; Kahn <n ⇒ cycle.

tradeoffs.topic: Block-then-BFS vs dodging bad cells during search
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Wall every neighbor of a bad cell first, then one reachability BFS from the start; do not try to dodge hazards inside the search (Solve The Maze).

tradeoffs.topic: Unused-node complement traversal vs materializing n^2 edges
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Keep an unused-node set and skip only explicit forbidden neighbors (The Two Routes / 0-1 MST); never build the dense complement.

tradeoffs.topic: Reverse multi-source BFS vs BFS from every query node
tradeoffs.strong_answer: For every v, nearest u with property P → BFS once from all P-nodes on the reversed graph (Nearest Opposite Parity), not a separate forward search per v.

tradeoffs.topic: Dual ready-queue Kahn vs single-queue Kahn
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Same indegree idea, different scheduler: maintain scarce vs free ready-queues, drain free repeatedly, then spend one scarce step (Coprocessor).

tradeoffs.topic: State/layered BFS vs rebuilding an explicit huge graph
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Use node=(v,state) for turns, hop parity, or layer mod 3 with a tiny state domain (Igor / Hopscotch Addict) instead of materializing layers.
If acyclic → 1 color; else 2 — mark DFS back-edges into the recursion stack (Coloring Edges).

gotchas.trap: Trying to avoid bad cells only while BFS runs.
gotchas.correction: First wall every neighbor of every bad cell, then check reachability of all goods (Solve The Maze).

gotchas.trap: Building the full complement adjacency for near-complete graphs.
gotchas.correction: Traverse an unused-node set and skip only the listed forbidden neighbors; cost O((n+m) log n).

gotchas.trap: Orienting an undirected graph for short directed paths without a bipartiteness check.
gotchas.correction: 2-color then orient every edge 0→1; impossible iff there is an odd cycle.

gotchas.trap: Putting a trap on every node of a functional-graph component.
gotchas.correction: Follow outdeg-1 edges; place the cheapest trap on each cycle only — inbound trees need nothing extra.

gotchas.trap: Answering nearest-opposite queries with forward BFS from each index.
gotchas.correction: Build the reverse jump graph and multi-source BFS from all odd and all even sinks.

gotchas.trap: Using a standard visited mark on Ice Cave’s destination.
gotchas.correction: Destination may be re-entered iff it has ≥2 open neighbors.

gotchas.trap: Running DAG path-count DP without detecting a cycle.
gotchas.correction: Fail cleanly if Kahn yields <n nodes before trusting longest-path or route counts.
